newsitem.title: UK: NatWest up on bid talk, positive comment.
newsitem.headline: NatWest up on bid talk, positive comment.

text.p: Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc rose on Monday amid positive analyst comment following press talk of a bid from or merger with banking rival Barclays Plc, dealers said.
"It's almost as if NatWest has run up the white flag," said one analyst.
"It seems like it will only be a matter of time before something happens. It has underperformed for ten years and major shareholders have had enough."
Goldman Sachs raised the stock to "market outperformer" from "market performer" and other brokerages including Panmure Gordon and Credit Lyonnais Laing were also positive on the stock.
NatWest shares were up 33p to 779-1/2 by 1241 GMT in active trade of just under nine million shares, putting it among the top ten most active UK shares at that time.

With NatWest weakened by recent turmoil in its investment banking arm, reports in the Guardian, Times and Wall Street Journal among others raised the prospect of a move involving Barclays -- while also pointing out the domestic regulatory obstacles.
A combination of the two should be able to cut costs in their UK branch network but would run into opposition because it would reduce the competition in lending to small businesses.

"If I was in (Barclays chief executive) Martin Taylor's shoes and I thought I could buy NatWest at its current price I would probably have a go," said Ian McEwan, analyst at Lehman Brothers. "But monopolies considerations would probably prevent it."

Reports earlier this month that NatWest had made an unsuccessful merger approach to Abbey National Plc had already stoked talk that NatWest could be at the heart of further consolidation in the UK bank sector.
Spokesmen for both NatWest and Barclays said they never commented on market speculation.
